title: Frontend senior scenario leading framework migration
topic: Frontend senior scenario leading framework migration
question: How would you approach leading this migration so the product keeps shipping and users aren't disrupted along the way?
idealAnswer:
Favor an incremental, coexistence-based approach over a big-bang rewrite, allowing old and new code to run side by side (e.g. behind feature flags, or route-by-route) so risk is spread out and partial progress still delivers value

Establish a clear migration order based on risk and blast radius, migrating lower-traffic or lower-risk areas first to build confidence and uncover unknowns before touching critical paths

Invest in automated tooling (codemods, lint rules) to handle mechanical parts of the migration at scale, rather than relying on every engineer manually applying the same repetitive change correctly

Communicate clearly with the other teams about the migration timeline, what patterns are now deprecated, and how their in-flight feature work should be written to avoid creating more migration debt

Set up strong automated test coverage and a rollback plan for each migrated slice, since with active concurrent development, catching regressions late is far more costly than catching them at merge time

Track and communicate progress with concrete, visible metrics, not just 'we're working on it', so the team and stakeholders can see real progress and adjust the plan if it stalls
